newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mozambique ready to help talks in Zaire - Chissano.
newsitem.headline: Mozambique ready to help talks in Zaire - Chissano.

text.p: Mozambique has no army to help refugees in Zaire, but the impoverished southeastern African nation would be willing to help with negotiations to end the regional crisis, its president said on Tuesday.

"We favour a peaceful resolution of the situation and are ready to contribute...primarily by providing an example of what we have done in Mozambique," President Joaquim Chissano told the French Institute for Foreign Relations (IFRI) as he began a visit to France.

Chissano, who arrived in France on Monday and leaves on Thursday, said Mozambique had learned a lot about resolving differences during three decades of conflict including a war of independence with Portugal and a civil war settled in 1992.
"We have no troops, but if we did we would be content to participate in the search for peace," he said, referring to a Paris proposal for a multinational force to help the refugees.
The force has yet to be approved by the United Nations Security Council.

Acknowledging his country is among the poorest in the world, Chissano said its economy had been growing steadily since 1993 and hoped to bring down inflation to between 15 percent and 27 percent this year from 70 percent three years ago.
